text:
Sarah N: FYI support escalated a high-p99 latency report from Acme (ticket #INC-9853). Customer saw p95 jump from ~120ms to ~2.4s and p99 > 12s for text-generation on their Dedicated pool this morning.
Cheng Li: Ugh. any obvious errors in provisioning? which pool?
Support Liaison: Dedicated pool id dp-02-west-eu, tenant acme-corp. They say the errors started around 10:05 UTC, coincides with a burst of traffic (~3x normal QPS).
Samir: Do we have attach/scaleup logs for dp-02-west-eu? I'm mostly worried about late-attach/cold GPU starts.
OpsBot: alert: dedicated-provisioning-queue-length dp-02-west-eu spike at 10:04 UTC -> +180 queued requests; attach-latency p95 6.8s.
Cheng Li: Can someone paste the autoscaler log lines for that period? I want to see backoffs and throttle messages.
Jonah: grabbing logs. quick grep: \n```\n2026-01-12T10:04:12Z autoscaler INFO queue_len=182 scaleup_attempt=1 backoff_ms=500 randomized_backoff=true\n2026-01-12T10:04:12Z provisioner WARN pool_capacity=0 requested_gpus=12 throttle=true\n2026-01-12T10:04:18Z provisioner INFO attach_started instance_id=i-0a1b2c attach_time_ms=3120\n2026-01-12T10:04:22Z attach-manager ERROR attach_timeout instance_id=i-0d4e5f\n```\nJonah: seems like a partial success then a bunch of timeouts.
Support Liaison: customer provided a sample request that reproduces the spike: 80 concurrent requests of long-sequence generation (max_tokens=2048) against model rdx-large-q8.
Sarah N: long seq + cold GPUs = expensive. But p95->2.4s is still bad even for long tokens. Might be queueing during warmup.
Cheng Li: Check kernel selection logs — sometimes the runtime picks a slower path during first warmups when memory pressure shows.
Samir: Also saw weird throttles on the dedicated-provisioning API: rate limit 120/min hit during burst. That made scaleup attempts get 429 then exponential backoff.
Cheng Li: That would explain delayed scale-up. Which means cold GPUs + throttled provisioning -> queue growth -> high p99.
Lucy: I pulled traces for a few requests. Here's a summarized trace for a slow request: \n- client -> front-end (20ms)\n- front-end routing (30ms)\n- queue wait (4.1s)\n- attach/warmup (3.2s)\n- runtime inference (150ms)\nTotal ~7.5s (matches customer p99 samples).
Sarah N: Repro steps (support recorded):\n1) Create sustained burst: 80 conn -> 10s sustained with max_tokens=2048 to rdx-large-q8\n2) Ensure pool dp-02-west-eu is at min_capacity=0 (they have no reserved capacity)\n3) Observe queue length and p99 jump within 30-90s
Samir: Thanks. I can repro locally by setting min_capacity=0 in a test pool and hammering with those requests. Good to know.
Cheng Li: Immediate mitigations we can push:\n- Short term: increase min_capacity for dp-02-west-eu to 2 GPUs for high-Tier tenants while we investigate (reduces cold start count).\n- Enable prioritized attach for SLA customers so provisioning API bypasses some rate limits.\n- Fallback: if attach latency > X, route tenant to a lower-size model (rdx-medium) automatically.
Lucy: We can also pre-warm kernels when a scale-up is initiated instead of waiting for first request to trigger heavy compilation. Might trade cost for latency but helps p99.
Support Liaison: Customer prefers a config change rather than code changes. They asked if we can bump min_capacity to avoid future incidents.
Jonah: I can apply min_capacity=2 as a temporary patch, but need approval from oncall (will increase cost).
Sarah N: Approved for the next 6 hours to calm the customer, set a reminder to roll back if not needed.
Samir: I'll add a rate-limit carveout for the dedicated-provisioning API for 10 minutes to let the backlog clear (ops only).
Cheng Li: For root cause, we should correlate: provisioning 429s -> autoscaler backoff -> queue growth -> attach storms -> attach timeouts. Long sequences exacerbate GPU warmup. Two-pronged fix: improve provisioning throughput and reduce cold GPU warmups.
Lucy: For longer-term: suggestions: proactive warm pools (keep small warm standby), randomized attach jitter (to avoid thundering herds), and cached kernel artifacts per pool flavor to cut warmup times.
Support Liaison: Customer happy with min_capacity change and temporary carveout. They've asked for a doc describing config knobs to avoid this in future (min_capacity, prewarm, model-fallback).
Sarah N: Action items:\n- Jonah: set min_capacity=2 for dp-02-west-eu now (DONE/rollback 6h)\n- Samir: apply temporary provisioning-rate carveout for acme-corp (ops ticket OP-4421)\n- Cheng: dig into provisioner 429s and propose capacity limit increase or split pool routing\n- Lucy: prototype kernel prewarm + artifact caching plan and rough cost estimate\n- Support Liaison: send customer postmortem + mitigation steps, ask if they want reserved capacity commit\nJonah: min_capacity change applied at 10:28 UTC. queue drained by 10:36 UTC. customer confirmed improved p95/p99 in their next sample.
Samir: carveout applied 10:30-10:40 UTC, ops ticket OP-4421 opened for longer-term policy.
Cheng Li: I'll take lead on investigating the 429 source. Initial hunch: misconfigured global rate limiter combined with sudden multi-tenant spikes.
Lucy: I'll start an RFC for prewarm+artifact cache; include cost/benefit and ops runbook.
Sarah N: Good triage — marking thread resolved for now. Reopen if customer sees regressions after rollback. :white_check_mark:
OpsBot: incident.note severity=medium action=min_capacity_patch responder=Jonah
